newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Wallis says prefers market forces.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Wallis says prefers market forces.

text.p: Stan Wallis, the chairman of the government's inquiry into the financial system, said on Wednesday he preferred market forces to determine the roles of financial service providers, rather than regulation.

"From the inquiry's perspective, we believe that it will best serve the interest of consumers and overall efficiency if the roles of different types of providers, including existing financial institutions, are allowed to be determined by market forces rather than by regulation," Wallis said in a speech to a conference on electronic commerce.
Wallis said new technology like the Internet and electronic cash could change the definition of a financial market.
"These possibilities could change the dynamics of competition in many areas of the financial system," he added.

Banks in favour of a relaxation of rules stopping the merger of Australias largest banks and insurance companies, like the National Australia Bank Ltd, have argued that new technology would create new competition. They have argued this new global competition for Australia's big four domestic banks and its two big superannuation and insurance groups meant a merger would not reduce competition.
